keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. Infobox 'Established: 11th century'; 'Their original territory was expansive, corresponding to much of what is now Mongolia'; Bartold (1913) 'located them along the upper Onon and Kherlen rivers and along the Tuul river'; Toghrul's forces 'dispersed throughout Central Mongolia' (Toghrul page). The 300 km radius around Ulan Bator is the Bartold reading, not the 'much of Mongolia' reading. The page gives no area. Revised after review: the 300 km circle used to take in 283 grid cells (about 72,000 km2, 42 percent of the merkit shape) of the Merkit land of the same years, Selenge and Bulgan provinces ('The Merkits lived in the basins of the Selenga and lower Orkhon River', Merkit page, merkit_1050); those two provinces are cut out. The Keraites page names only the upper Onon, the Kherlen and the Tuul and has no word on the Selenga or a boundary with the Merkits; the cut is the Merkit dossier's land.

ledger.note: c. 1000: the Keraites enter the Church of the East. 'They were absorbed into the Church of the East around 1000 by Metropolitan Abdisho' and 'converted ... early in the 11th century'; the infobox starts the Keraites in the 11th century; the page's predecessors are the Zubu and the Kara-Khanid Khanate.

ledger.note: 1203: Temüjin defeats the Keraites. 'In 1203, Temüjin defeated the Keraites, who were distracted by the collapse of their coalition'; 'They were defeated by Genghis Khan in 1203'; Toghrul fled to the Naimans and was killed by a Naiman soldier who did not recognize him (Toghrul page). The majority 'allied themselves with Temüjin'.

wars.note: The Keraites page says the Keraites 'were gradually absorbed into the succeeding Mongol khanates during the 13th century'.

wars.name: Kerait-Mongol campaign against the Naimans
wars.outcome: 'In 1199, Temüjin together with an ally Ong khan launched a campaign against the Naimans' (Naimans page, read in the naiman dossier); the Toghrul page: 'Around 1199, Toghrul wanted to finish once and for all with the Naimans.' No land is recorded.

certainty.note: A steppe khanate known from a few river names; no border on any page.

notes: New state (Cliopatria lacks the Keraites). The infobox lists 'Subject to: Liao dynasty, Qara Khitai (Western Liao), Genghisids' and the page has them 'in union with the Khitan' vassals of the Kara-Khitai state: no dates, so the dossier carries no vassal events; the kara-khitans and liao-dynasty dossiers could add them. The page gives the Jin title in 1196 where the Toghrul page puts the 'Wang Khan' name in the 1194 campaign against the Tatars. Markus Buyruk Khan was killed by the Liao in 1100. Cliopatria's Mongol Empire begins in 1206, leaving 1203-1206. The pages call the Keraite territory 'much of what is now Mongolia' but name only the Tuul, Kherlen and Onon, which the keyframe follows. Merkit, Tatar and Jalayir peoples of the same age have no page read here. Gazetteer names used (Ulaanbaatar) resolve. REVISED after review (ia-01-x fix pass): the shape no longer overlaps the merkit dossier (Selenge and Bulgan provinces are subtracted in the keyframe, both ledger events, the successor land and the Burning Sands war zone); the Keraites page (re-read) mentions the Merkits only in lists of peoples and gives no boundary. Page re-read for the thin points: the capital 'Orta Balagasun' (probably 'in an old Uyghur or Khitan fortress') has no location on the page, so no capital with coordinates can be added beyond the Ulan Bator palace; Liao and Qara Khitai vassalage is undated ('In union with the Khitan, they became vassals of the Kara-Khitai state'; Toghrul page: no vassalage stated), so no vassal events; the Toghrul page gives his reign as 1165-1194 and 1198-1203 (overthrown by Erke Qara after 1194, 'The Keraites returned fully to Toghrul around 1198') and an undated stay with the Qara Khitai, which move no land and are not events here. Four grid cells (about 1,000 km2) still lie in both shapes (the Merkit circle round Ulan-Ude touches the Kerait circle); the Merkit shape also reaches Ulan-Ude (south Buryatia), outside the Kerait circle.
